content: 1. If the initial dose of dasatinib was 70 mg daily, reduce the dose to 20 mg orally daily. If dasatinib is not tolerated after dose reduction, consider alternative therapies. If mifepristone is discontinued, wait approximately one week before increasing the dasatinib dose. 2. Mifepristone and deflazacort are contraindicated due to an unknown mechanism. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the deflazacort dose by one-third and monitor closely. 3. Mifepristone and degarelix require close monitoring due to potential QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 4. Mifepristone and desflurane both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 5. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of desipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or use alternatives if available. 6. Mifepristone decreases the effects of desogestrel through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 7. Mifepristone increases the levels of deuruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Deuruxolitinib should not be used with strong or moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors. 8. Mifepristone and deutetrabenazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 9. Mifepristone and dexamethasone are contraindicated due to an unknown mechanism. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 10. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of diazepam (oral, buccal, or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 11. Mifepristone and dichlorphenamide both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of diclofenac (topical) by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9 metabolism. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor closely. 13. Mifepristone decreases the effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 14. Mifepristone increases the levels of dihydroergotamine (oral or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 15. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Co-administration may increase plasma concentrations of diltiazem. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 16. Mifepristone and disopyramide require close monitoring due to potential QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for docetaxel-related adverse reactions. Consider a 50% dose reduction of docetaxel if chronic mifepristone use is necessary. The clinical significance of this interaction with short-term mifepristone use for pregnancy termination is unknown. 18. Mifepristone and dofetilide require close monitoring due to potential QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of mifepristone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 19. Mifepristone and dolasetron require close monitoring due to potential QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 20. Mifepristone and donepezil both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 22. Mifepristone and doxepin (oral or cream) both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 23. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Mifepristone and dronedarone are contraindicated due to QTc interval prolongation. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 26. Mifepristone and droperidol require close monitoring due to potential QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 27. Mifepristone decreases the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. 28. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, which may increase the risk of toxicities. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates and monitor for signs of toxicity. 29. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 30. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 31. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases the levels of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 32. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 35. Mifepristone increases the levels of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 36. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 37. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. 38. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase free MMAE exposure, leading to increased toxicity. 39. Mifepristone and enoxaparin are contraindicated due to the risk of excessive post-abortion bleeding in patients on anticoagulant therapy. 40. Mifepristone and entrectinib both increase the QTc interval. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 41. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 42. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 44. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates, ergonovine, and ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 45. Mifepristone and eribulin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 46. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the erlotinib dose by 50 mg increments if severe reactions occur. The clinical significance of this interaction with short-term mifepristone use is unknown. 47. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base and erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs.
